newsitem.title: USA: Bankrupt Discovery Zone to play in junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: Bankrupt Discovery Zone to play in junk bonds.

text.p: Discovery Zone Inc, the insolvent indoor play center company, will look to the junk bond market to finance its emergence from bankruptcy, according to sources familiar with the transaction.
The company plans to sell $85 million in five-year senior secured notes via Jefferies and Co Inc in a 144A private placement toward the end of July, the sources said.
To increase investor interest, the company is also expected to give bondholders an undisclosed amount of equity in the new company in the form of warrants, they said.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to pay back a debtor-in-possession facility, cover administrative fees and expenses, and then to finance Discovery Zone's turaround plan.
The company will be raising an additional $15 million through a private placement of preferred stock, the sources said.
Company officials declined comment due to Securities and Exchange Commission disclosure restrictions.

Discovery Zone, which once had a stock market value totalling $1.3 billion, filed for bankruptcy in March 1996. A hearing on its reorganization plan, which will include details of the high-yield financing, is scheduled for July 18.

After emerging from bankruptcy, Discovery Zone will be controlled by Martin Davis, former chairman of Paramount Communications Inc, and a group of investors. The group gained control of the company by buying its bank debt at a deep discount.
Owners of trade receivables and certain other debt obligations will receive a minority equity stake in the new company.
Discovery Zone, based in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., operates 208 indoor play centers around the country.
Last December Viacom Inc wrote off its 49 percent investment in Discovery Zone, which it owned through its Blockbuster Entertainment unit. Viacom no longer owns a stake in the company.
